ShortDescription.Value: Make pedestrian crossings as wide as you like, from one slider. More paint on the junction, and room for people to cross side by side.

Publish.LongDescription:
# Crosswalk Width
Crossings in Cities: Skylines II are a thin painted band that a queue of citizens shuffles across in single file. This puts a slider on how wide they are.
## What it does
Crossing width becomes a percentage of whatever the crossing was drawn with, so a side street keeps a modest crossing and a boulevard keeps a generous one — everything scales together. A floor and a ceiling in metres are there for the cases where a proportion is not what you want.
Widening a crossing widens both halves of it at once: the painted zebra covers more of the junction, and the strip people walk on gets wider, so a crowd spreads across it instead of filing over.
## How it works
A crossing is not part of the road's cross-section — it is a lane laid across the carriageway, and the painted zebra is that lane's mesh. This mod changes the width of that lane on the game's own lane prefabs and lets the game lay the crossings. No geometry of its own, no Harmony patches, and the road itself never gets wider.
## Applying it
Crossings laid after you change the setting are correct immediately. Ones already standing were laid at the old width — reload the save, or press "Apply to existing crossings" to re-lay them in place.
Removing the mod puts every crossing back to the width its asset author chose.
Publish.ChangeLog: 1.0.0 First release. Crossing width as a percentage of the crossing's own, with an optional minimum and maximum in metres. Widens the painted band and the walking strip together. Crossings already laid can be re-laid from the settings panel.
